description:
This adds toggle` and `togglelocal` command as requested here https://github.com/zyedidia/micro/issues/2086.
Not sure if this is the most correct approach, I found settings code a bit confusing and with non-intuitive variable names and behaviors.
Feedback is appreciated.

comments.body: Just "Not enough arguments", for consistency with other commands (including `togglelocal`?
We can just use type assertion.
We can just use `SetGlobalOptionNative()`. No point in converting it to string just to convert it back from string inside `SetGlobalOption()`.
Maybe "toggles a boolean option"?
Just "toggles the option on/off"?
The options help refers to their values mostly as `true` and `false`, not `on` and `off`... Instead of this entire sentence "See the...", maybe just "Only works with boolean options"?
Options here are in alphabetical order, let's not break it...
Wdym "options here" are you refering to the fact I moved `show` and `reset`?

Seems good, I'll change it.

Your comment made me wonder, maybe we could improve the toggle suggestions - i.e. when the user types `toggle` and hit tab the options that show up as suggestions are only boolean options. You think it would be a good idea? Maybe it's a problem for another PR, it could be done also for `setlocal`.
I was being consistent but with `ShowKeyCmd` and `ShowCmd` :rofl:

Surely sounds like a good idea.

Side note: I've just tried using `setlocal` for a global-only option (`infobar`), and (besides the fact that it shows up among suggestions), the error displayed after `setlocal infobar off` is: `Invalid option`. It would be nice to make it more informative / less confusing, to make it clear why it is invalid in this case.

Side note 2: I've just taken a glance at the code in `OptionValueComplete()`, what a mess.

Ah sorry, somehow I was thinking that this is `help options` (where all options are indeed listed in alphabetical order), but this is `help commands`... Ok, then no issue, quite the  opposite, it's better to keep related options close together, rather than have them in a completely arbitrary order.

Ye, I got confused plenty of times as well with settings code in general. 
Starting with, a setting can be `global` or `local` but then we have 	`GlobalSettings map[string]interface{}` at first sight I'd say its a list of global-only settings, but it's, in fact, a list of all settings. Inside there's `a list of settings that should never be globally modified`. Why not call it just `Settings` or `AllSettings`?

Makes sense, I took a look at `SetGlobalOptionNative` and it feels off calling it directly.

Although is a function exposed to lua side it doesn't make options verification nor type verification. 
I've tested with lua, (afaics),  you can do this with no errors:
config.SetGlobalOptionNative("fakecursor", "cutelisp")
config.SetGlobalOptionNative("notanoption", "maluka")

> Surely sounds like a good idea.

Thinking in advance I could already create a function `isBooleanOption(opt) boolean`to use on `toggleCmd` & `toggleLocalCmd` and in the future on the suggestion logic, wt do you think?

Indeed, another example of a mess. One would intuitively expect that `config.OptionIsValid()` would take care of that, but it doesn't.

Well, we expose a lot of dangerous stuff to lua, as a matter of fact.

Anyway, even if we don't want to modify `SetGlobalOptionNative()` now, we can easily use if safely here, ~~just by validating if `newVal` is boolean too, right?~~ wtf I'm saying, don't even need to validate it, if `oldVal` is boolean, `!oldVal` is boolean too, right?
I'm not sure what for.
Ye, I was just pointing out. In this case won't be harmful since I'll check option and value before calling `SetGlobalOptionNative()`

I think it's better to use `h.Buf.Settings[option]`, not just to avoid confusion when reading the code (although I understand the cause of this confusion is the confusing name of `GetGlobalOption()`, not your code), but also to check if this not a global-only option. With your current version, `togglelocal infobar` silently "succeeds" (and then `show infobar` meaninglessly says that infobar is false for this buffer). In comparison,  `setlocal infobar off` correctly fails and shows an error message (albeit perhaps not the clearest one).
Again, why not just "toggles the option on/off" (without backquotes), i.e. just use human language here?
Please remove unneeded spaces (and generally, use `gofmt`).
Just noticed (thanks to `git show`): unneeded trailing spaces added here.

This line is a bit too long, please split (and perhaps line 75 too). As you may notice, we try to keep the maximum width of lines in the documentation to be under 80 characters (well, sometimes just a bit above 80 characters).

diff --git a/runtime/help/commands.md b/runtime/help/commands.md

    current buffer). This will *not* modify `settings.json`.
 
-* `toggle 'option'`: toggles the option true/false. Only works with boolean options.
-   This will modify your `settings.json` with the new value.

+   options. This will modify your `settings.json` with the new value.
 
-* `togglelocal 'option'`: toggles the option true/false locally
-   (only in the current buffer). Only works with boolean options.
-   This will *not* modify `settings.json`.
+* `togglelocal 'option'`: toggles the option true/false locally (only in the

nit: missing space before parenthesis. :)

I can remember https://github.com/zyedidia/micro/pull/3021#issuecomment-1806536539 :wink: 
Is there really the need to limit the (local) toggling to boolean options, since we could cycle through the other as well?

>  cycle through the other

What other means here? Every option?
Every option isn't possible, since we've integers and custom strings as well, but `OptionChoices` and `colorscheme` are additionally toggle-able...at least from my perspective.

Erm, from my POV, a toggle would be on/off. I think the only non-boolean toggleable options are `fileformat` and `helpsplit` from `OptionChoices`.

Aside from naming, I don't think creating a cycling command would be useful. We could make options with exactly two values toggleable, though.

Going further, we could enhance `RegisterCommonOption` and `RegisterGlobalOption` to accept option choices directly (and other verifications?).
Cycling through colorschemes with a command/keybinding might be nice but I agree that wouldn't really be called "toggling" any more.

Just out of curiosity, what's the use case? I really don't see any utility in cycling, the only thing I can think of is a "colorscheme menu".

BTW, cycling through colorschemes is already possible in lua.

> Just out of curiosity, what's the use case?

Cycling through all the colorschemes is something you do occasionally to either pick the one you like the best or to check that they all work as expected. I know it can be done in a plugin but having it built-in could help new users pick a colorscheme.

I'm not sure if it is worth implementing, but if it is I definitely think it shouldn't be part of the `toggle` command.

Ohh I see.

> could help new users pick a colorscheme.

Surely, selecting 1 by 1 is a PITA. But in this case I think a colorscheme preview suits more into this problem. It was already requested https://github.com/zyedidia/micro/issues/1782 https://github.com/zyedidia/micro/issues/2677

> I can remember [#3021 (comment)](https://github.com/zyedidia/micro/pull/3021#issuecomment-1806536539) 😉

Actually prior to that comment there was this discussion: https://github.com/zyedidia/micro/pull/2876#issuecomment-1803733078

starting from this comment of mine:

> One note though: perhaps it's better to go a simpler route and, instead of this "generic and extensible" `matchbracestyle` option with `highlight` and `underline` values, add a simple boolean option e.g. `matchbracehighlight`? An advantage is that, if we implement a generic support for easy toggling on/off arbitrary options (see https://github.com/zyedidia/micro/issues/2086), then it will be readily usable for this `matchbracehighlight` option as well, to easily toggle between highlighting and underlining.

And now, I tend to agree with @cutelisp and @Andriamanitra that `toggle` for options with 3 or more choices would be rather weird [*]. But, for options with exactly 2 choices, like this `matchbracestyle`, it seems like a nice idea indeed. And that would also address precisely the concern from my quoted comment above.

[*] Even though, as I've realized just now, it was me who suggested that stupid idea, in https://github.com/zyedidia/micro/pull/2876#issuecomment-1806555253.
I'll give it a try on including "2-choice options"

Ok, you guys convinced me.
We give it a try for the "2-choice options". :+1:
Should we bother saying it's an invalid option or should we just say it's not a toggleable option anyway.
At this position it is invalid.
Indeed, looks like we can simplify that and just switch based on `if !local {}` without fallback.

Right. 
As I pointed [here](https://github.com/zyedidia/micro/pull/3783#discussion_r2167866732) `SetGlobalOptionNative` has some odd behavior.  I just realized that, with the current logic, setting a global-only value it also populates the `Settings` field of each buffer in `openBuffers`. IMO, the current variable and function names related to settings are misleading, and we should consider renaming them if we eventually patch these functions.

> The point is what is invalid? An invalid option or a invalid option **for this command**?

When `toggleOption()` is called with `local` set to `false` and calls `config.GetGlobalOption(option)` with a `option` not tracked within, then it is indeed an ErrInvalidOption. If it is toggleable will be checked later on.

`GetGlobalOption()` is already exported to plugins:
https://github.com/zyedidia/micro/blob/dbdf753f27dd6686034e0dd09b975f3377ebe743/cmd/micro/initlua.go#L90

> `GetGlobalOption()` is already exported to plugins:

Yes, and used on go side as well. Thats why `GetGlobalOption*`, it would be a different function.
Note that we already use this logic.
```go
if _, ok := config.GlobalSettings[option]; !ok {
  return config.ErrInvalidOption
}
```


> When `toggleOption()` is called with `local` set to `false` and calls `config.GetGlobalOption(option)` with a `option` not tracked within, then it is indeed an ErrInvalidOption. If it is toggleable will be checked later on.

I am aware, the edge case comes when we call it with `local` set to `true` and we give a valid global-only option.
`(b *Buffer) GetOption()` would handle it with a specific error
